title: Subjuntivo de duda: no está claro que...

sections.content: Expressions of doubt or improbability -- no es evidente que, dudo que, no parece probable que, es poco probable que -- all trigger the subjunctive, the natural mood for a historian hedging a claim about how solid a social category really was. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: No es evidente que esta nueva clase media compartiera una identidad tan clara como la de la vieja oligarquía terrateniente.
items.english: It's not obvious that this new middle class shared as clear an identity as that of the old landed oligarchy.

items.spanish: Dudo que un abogado, un maestro de escuela y un empleado de banco se hubieran visto a sí mismos, en 1890, como parte de un mismo grupo social.
items.english: I doubt that a lawyer, a schoolteacher and a bank clerk would have seen themselves, in 1890, as part of the same social group.

items.spanish: No parece probable que la vieja élite terrateniente imaginara, a mediados de siglo, esta clase de competencia.
items.english: It doesn't seem likely that the old landed elite imagined, by mid-century, this kind of competition.

items.spanish: Es poco probable que estas nuevas clases sociales se hubieran formado con la misma rapidez sin el auge exportador.
items.english: It's unlikely that these new social classes would have formed as quickly without the export boom.

sections.content: Compare es poco probable que (subjunctive, doubt) with es cierto que / está claro que (indicative, certainty) -- the same fact can be framed either way, and the mood you choose signals how confident the writer actually is.
